change: Graduate route duration for non-doctoral graduates falls from 2 years to 18 months
affected_cohort: Eligible Graduate route applications submitted on/after 2027-01-01; doctoral graduates remain at 3 years
observed_fact: UK Immigration Rules set 18 months for applications from 1 Jan 2027, versus 2 years before that date
pathway_mechanism: Shortens job-search window before needing a sponsored or other eligible route
directional_eom_impact: Negative for post-study transition flexibility; no numeric energy change assigned
counterfactual_or_caveat: Scotland/Edinburgh uses the UK immigration route; local labour demand and programme outcomes are separate

change: DHS proposes OPT fees of USD 70,000 for initial OPT and USD 30,000 for subsequent OPT
effective_date: Not effective; depends on final rule
affected_cohort: F-1 students seeking OPT if proposal is finalized as written; fee payer/designated institution mechanics require tracking
observed_fact: Federal Register published the DHS proposed rule on 2026-10-08: $70,000 initial OPT fee and $30,000 for subsequent OPT recommendations. Proposed only, not in force; comments due 2026-11-09. The fee would be paid by the SEVP-certified school before its recommendation.
pathway_mechanism: Could sharply reduce employers' or schools' willingness to support OPT, undermining post-study work feasibility
directional_eom_impact: Large negative scenario risk, but no baseline energy adjustment until final rule/status is known
counterfactual_or_caveat: No new fee applies today. Final rule could be revised, withdrawn or challenged; proposed effective date would be 60 days after a final rule is published.

change: Student visa fee rises from AUD 2,000 to AUD 2,500; Temporary Graduate visa fee rises from AUD 4,600 to AUD 5,750
affected_cohort: Applications lodged on/after 2026-07-01, subject to stated concessions
observed_fact: Study Australia reports both fee increases effective 1 July 2026
pathway_mechanism: Raises up-front and post-study pathway costs; small negative affordability effect
directional_eom_impact: Negative on cost component; not enough to justify country reranking alone
counterfactual_or_caveat: Does not remove graduate work rights; visa duration/eligibility depends on existing subclass rules

change: Eligible post-secondary students no longer need a separate co-op work permit for required placements
affected_cohort: Eligible post-secondary international students in required co-op/internship/practicum placements
observed_fact: IRCC says a separate co-op work permit is no longer required from 1 April 2026 for eligible placements
pathway_mechanism: Reduces placement paperwork during study; does not itself extend post-study work or PR access
directional_eom_impact: Small positive programme-friction effect; no broad settlement-score change
counterfactual_or_caveat: Do not confuse with PGWP eligibility or long-term settlement reforms

change: Employment Pass minimum qualifying salary rises from SGD 5,600 to SGD 6,000 (most sectors); financial services SGD 6,200 to SGD 6,600
affected_cohort: New EP applicants from 2027 and renewals for passes expiring from 2028
observed_fact: Singapore MOM announced the thresholds and dates
pathway_mechanism: Raises salary floor for employer-sponsored professional entry; may favour higher-paid roles and increase threshold friction
directional_eom_impact: Negative for marginal salary offers; mixed for experienced tech professionals with high salary potential
counterfactual_or_caveat: COMPASS still applies; sector and age affect actual qualifying salary

change: Opposition proposal to sharply reduce migration and abolish temporary graduate visas for most students
status: Political proposal only; not current law
effective_date: None; contingent on election and legislation
affected_cohort: Potential future international students and temporary graduate visa applicants if enacted
observed_fact: Media reports describe a Coalition proposal; it has not changed current visa rules
pathway_mechanism: If enacted without an equivalent alternative, could weaken post-study bridge to sponsored work
directional_eom_impact: Downside scenario only; no baseline energy adjustment
counterfactual_or_caveat: Keep separate from enacted subclass 485 rules and official current visa fees

change: Non-school international student transfer restriction temporarily extended from 6 to 12 months
affected_cohort: Non-school overseas students seeking to transfer from one registered provider to another during the temporary period
observed_fact: Providers are prohibited from knowingly enrolling a transferring student before 12 months of their principal course are completed with the current provider
pathway_mechanism: Raises switching friction if a programme/provider proves unsuitable; increases importance of validating programme quality and course fit before enrolment
directional_eom_impact: Small negative for flexibility and downside-risk management; no broad destination score adjustment
counterfactual_or_caveat: Temporary measure through 2027-06-30; does not itself remove post-study work rights or change permanent-residence criteria

change: Graduate Diploma of Management (Learning), BSB80120, CRICOS registration suspended/cancelled for new enrolments
affected_cohort: Prospective overseas students seeking to enrol in this specified course; existing students may complete
observed_fact: Australian Department of Education says new overseas enrolments in the specified course are not permitted from 5 October 2026 because of systemic integrity concerns
pathway_mechanism: Highlights course-level provider/qualification integrity risk; reinforces checking CRICOS status, accreditation and genuine programme outcomes before paying deposits
directional_eom_impact: No national attractiveness score change; positive evidence for a programme-quality screening rule
counterfactual_or_caveat: This is a specific Graduate Diploma course action, not a ban on Australian MBA or master's programmes generally

change: Student-route maintenance funds uplifted for the 2026/27 academic year
affected_cohort: Student-route applications governed by Immigration Rules taking effect on 8 October 2026, subject to transitional provisions
observed_fact: HC 584 updates the student maintenance requirement to align with the 2026/27 home-student maintenance-loan level; exact personal evidence requirement depends on course duration and whether studying in London
pathway_mechanism: Raises documented funds required before study, increasing liquidity/cash-planning burden
directional_eom_impact: Small negative on upfront liquidity; no score adjustment without exact applicable amount and user's programme/location
counterfactual_or_caveat: Do not confuse the maintenance-funds evidence requirement with tuition or actual living expenditure; Scotland follows UK immigration rules

change: Student sponsor compliance guidance updated; expanded RAG rating and enforcement clarifications
status: Official guidance update; underlying thresholds already effective
effective_date: Guidance version updated 2026-10-09; core thresholds apply to assessments from 2026-06-01; completion threshold rises from 2027-06-01
affected_cohort: UK Student-route sponsor institutions and prospective/current international students at those institutions
observed_fact: Home Office guidance updated 9 Oct 2026. For assessments from 1 Jun 2026: visa refusal rate must be below 5%, enrolment rate at least 95%, and course completion at least 85%; for assessments from Jun 2027, completion threshold becomes at least 90%. The updated guidance clarifies the RAG framework and how some withdrawals and repeated discretionary assessments are treated.
pathway_mechanism: Provider compliance may affect licence continuity, international recruitment and student continuity; increases the value of checking sponsor status, completion rates and institutional financial/operational resilience before paying a deposit.
directional_eom_impact: Negative for provider-level downside risk where compliance is weak; no evidence supports a blanket negative energy adjustment for the whole UK or Scotland.
counterfactual_or_caveat: This is provider-level compliance, not a new general student eligibility rule. It should affect institution/programme risk assessment, not automatically rerank all UK destinations.

change: Bloomsbury Institute student sponsor licence revoked after failing Basic Compliance Assessment
status: Official enforcement example; historical event added to evidence log
affected_cohort: New international students seeking sponsorship at the named provider; some existing sponsored students faced potential transfer or alternative-route needs
observed_fact: Home Office reported that the provider failed the Basic Compliance Assessment and was removed from the Register of Student Sponsors; existing students were not affected immediately, but a small number could need to transfer or use another eligible route.
pathway_mechanism: Demonstrates that institution-level sponsor status can create material continuity risk even where the national Student route remains open.
directional_eom_impact: Raises the priority of institution-level quality and sponsor checks; no country-wide energy change assigned.
counterfactual_or_caveat: Single-provider enforcement event; not a measure of sector-wide revocation frequency or a reason to avoid the UK as a whole.

change: Reported university withdrawals of international student offers amid tighter visa-refusal compliance threshold
status: Secondary-source education-market signal; not a separate policy rule
effective_date: Reported response during 2026; no separate legal effective date
affected_cohort: The report highlights applicants from Pakistan, Nigeria and Bangladesh; impact on Indian applicants is not quantified
observed_fact: Financial Times reported on 11 Oct 2026 that universities were withdrawing some international offers to avoid breaching the sponsor visa-refusal threshold; it reported withdrawn applications rising to 10.5% in H1 2026 from 2.3% in 2025. These are reported figures, not a newly downloaded official series.
pathway_mechanism: Potentially increases admissions uncertainty and makes university-specific sponsor compliance, offer conditions and refund rules more important.
directional_eom_impact: Small negative risk signal for UK admissions/provider continuity; no UK/Scotland reranking because India-specific effects and programme-level data are missing.
counterfactual_or_caveat: Secondary report behind a paywall; the named high-withdrawal origin cohorts are not India, so do not infer the same withdrawal rate for Indian applicants.

change: Student visa onshore application and family-member rules tightened under 2026 student visa integrity reforms
status: Implemented rule; official government explainer checked 2026-10-13
affected_cohort: Most temporary visa holders applying for Student visa onshore; student visa holders seeking another Student visa (subject to exemptions); most new/further Student visa applicants seeking to include family members; current Student visas unaffected
observed_fact: From 2 Oct 2026, most temporary visa holders cannot apply for Student visa while in Australia; student visa holders generally cannot apply for another onshore Student visa unless exempt; most applicants cannot include/add family members except specified exemptions. Existing Student visas unaffected.
pathway_mechanism: Raises friction for onshore course/visa switching and narrows family accompaniment in the study stage; direct offshore application from India is not itself prohibited.
directional_eom_impact: Qualitative upward energy (weaker attractor) for applicants relying on onshore switching or family accompaniment; little direct effect on initial offshore application; no numeric score assigned.
counterfactual_or_caveat: Transfer stream details still under development; Temporary Graduate visa family restrictions still being progressed. Official guidance says current Student visas are unaffected.

change: Student sponsor guidance and student sponsor register updated
effective_date: 2026-10-09 (publication/update date; specific rules depend on the relevant Immigration Rules changes)
affected_cohort: Prospective international students choosing a UK education provider
observed_fact: GOV.UK records Student sponsor guidance updated 9 Oct 2026 and the Student sponsor register dated 9 Oct 2026.
pathway_mechanism: Makes provider due diligence and sponsor status checking particularly important before paying a deposit; does not by itself mean a named programme lost sponsorship
directional_eom_impact: Provider-specific diligence risk; no national numeric energy change assigned
counterfactual_or_caveat: Verify the exact university and course arrangements with the institution and current official register; Edinburgh follows UK immigration rules

change: Official monthly visa applications: sponsored study applications lower year-on-year
status: Official provisional statistics; demand indicator, not a policy change
affected_cohort: All sponsored study main applicants; not India-only and not programme-specific
observed_fact: 352,500 sponsored study visa applications in the year ending September 2026, 19% lower than the year ending September 2025; student dependant applications 15,700, down 31%.
pathway_mechanism: Signals lower application volume and potentially changing international-study demand; it does not establish admission, visa approval, job prospects or causal effects of a single policy.
directional_eom_impact: Ambiguous mild upward energy risk signal for UK/Scotland study demand; no numeric score assigned because applications are not an attractiveness or success rate.
counterfactual_or_caveat: Provisional rolling 12-month totals, seasonality and multiple policy/economic drivers; do not insert as a calendar-year flow or interpret as approvals.

change: Official monthly Skilled Worker visa applications lower year-on-year
status: Official provisional statistics; labour-migration pipeline indicator
affected_cohort: Skilled Worker main applicants across occupations and nationalities
observed_fact: 26,400 Skilled Worker visa applications in the year ending September 2026, 43% lower than the year ending September 2025.
pathway_mechanism: Possible signal of lower sponsored-work route volume; not a count of tech jobs or an employer sponsorship success rate.
directional_eom_impact: Mild upward energy risk signal for post-study sponsorship access, but direction is not conclusive; no numeric score assigned.
counterfactual_or_caveat: Occupation mix, salary thresholds, policy changes and application timing affect the series. No technology-specific breakdown used here.

change: New Short-Term Graduate Work Visa and expanded graduate-diploma PSWV eligibility announced
affected_cohort: Eligible Level 5–7 graduates who do not qualify for a PSWV; some Level 7 graduate-diploma holders with a bachelor degree
observed_fact: A six-month open-work visa will be available to specified graduates from 16 Nov 2026; Level 7 graduate diploma graduates with a bachelor degree may qualify for PSWV up to the time studied, capped at one year.
pathway_mechanism: Adds a limited job-search bridge for certain non-MBA qualification cohorts and broadens eligibility for some graduate diploma holders.
directional_eom_impact: No meaningful change for the target Tech MBA pathway; likely not applicable to a standard MBA qualification. No score assigned.
counterfactual_or_caveat: Do not confuse this six-month route with the main Post-Study Work Visa; family support is restricted on the short-term visa.

change: Immigration Rules amendments HC 584; updates affect Government Authorised Exchange, Hong Kong BN(O), long residence, family and related provisions
status: Official rules update; provision-specific commencement dates
affected_cohort: Only applicants covered by the amended appendices/provisions; not a general Skilled Worker change
observed_fact: Home Office Immigration Rules updates page records amendments published 8 October 2026 reflecting Statement of Changes HC 584; parliamentary statement says some changes commence on 8 October, 29 October, 30 November and 9 December 2026.
pathway_mechanism: May change eligibility or administrative rules for specified exchange placements, BN(O), long-residence and family cohorts; exact direction depends on provision and applicant cohort.
directional_eom_impact: No general numeric energy adjustment; scenario-specific policy feature only after affected route and mechanism are mapped.
counterfactual_or_caveat: Do not treat this as a broad change to the Skilled Worker route or as evidence of changed migration flows. Separate publication date from each provision effective date.

change: Recognised modern-slavery victims on Skilled Worker visas can leave abusive sponsors and work for any employer for the remainder of their visa
affected_cohort: Skilled Worker visa holders formally recognised by the Home Office as modern-slavery victims
observed_fact: Home Office states recognised victims are no longer tied to the specific sponsor and may take any lawful work for the remainder of existing permission.
pathway_mechanism: Reduces sponsor lock-in and downside risk for a narrow, vulnerable cohort; may improve ability to switch jobs after recognition.
directional_eom_impact: Potentially lowers effective labour-access/friction energy for this cohort; no numeric score applied.
counterfactual_or_caveat: Not a general relaxation of Skilled Worker switching rules; do not extrapolate to all sponsored workers or all migrant profiles.

change: ONE Pass (AI and Tech) track announced; intended to replace Tech.Pass from January 2027
affected_cohort: Highly paid AI/technology leaders and senior technical talent meeting company and experience criteria
observed_fact: MOM says the track will accept a combination of cash and assessed vested non-cash compensation for the salary criterion; published criteria include high compensation and at least five years of relevant experience.
pathway_mechanism: May increase flexibility for a narrow high-end talent segment while leaving most ordinary work-pass applicants outside this route.
directional_eom_impact: Potentially lowers access friction for eligible top AI/tech talent; no broad destination energy change assigned.
counterfactual_or_caveat: Eligibility is highly selective; future rules and implementation details can change. This is not a general work-visa liberalisation.

change: Employment Pass and S Pass qualifying salary thresholds scheduled to increase for new applications
affected_cohort: New Employment Pass and S Pass applications from January 2027; renewals for passes expiring from January 2028
observed_fact: MOM announced minimum EP salary increasing from SGD 5,600 to 6,000 (financial services 6,200 to 6,600) and S Pass from SGD 3,300 to 3,600 (financial services 3,800 to 4,000), with age-graded thresholds.
pathway_mechanism: Raises the salary hurdle for some employer-sponsored applicants while maintaining higher salary norms and targeting workforce composition.
directional_eom_impact: Potentially increases entry friction for candidates near the old thresholds; may be neutral for applicants well above thresholds. No numeric score assigned.
counterfactual_or_caveat: Future effective date; do not apply these thresholds to applications before the stated dates or treat them as observed migration outcomes.

change: Minimum annual remuneration thresholds increased for employment permits
affected_cohort: New employment permit applicants in relevant permit categories, subject to category-specific rules and phased changes
observed_fact: Government roadmap raised the General Employment Permit minimum from EUR 34,000 to EUR 36,605 and Critical Skills Employment Permit minimum from EUR 38,000 to EUR 40,904 from 1 March 2026.
pathway_mechanism: Raises the wage/eligibility hurdle for jobs below the new thresholds; may also reduce undercutting and align thresholds with wage growth.
directional_eom_impact: Potentially raises access-friction energy for lower-paid eligible applicants; no numeric score assigned.
counterfactual_or_caveat: Thresholds are permit-specific and have further phased changes through 2030; eligibility and exemptions must be modelled by route and occupation.

change: 2026 Express Entry category-based selection priorities published
status: Current selection framework; invitations depend on rounds and eligibility
affected_cohort: Eligible Express Entry candidates in category-based rounds
observed_fact: IRCC added categories including doctors, researchers and senior managers with Canadian work experience, transport occupations, and skilled military recruits with a job offer; renewed categories include French, health/social services, education, STEM and trades.
pathway_mechanism: Changes the relative invitation opportunities for candidates who meet targeted category criteria; it does not guarantee invitation or permanent residence.
directional_eom_impact: Potentially improves relative pathway attractiveness for eligible profiles; not a uniform positive shift for all applicants.
counterfactual_or_caveat: Category-based selection supplements other rounds; actual selection depends on CRS scores, category eligibility and invitation rounds. No numeric score assigned.

change: Opposition proposal to reduce temporary visa numbers and alter student/graduate pathways reported
status: Opposition proposal; not enacted government policy
affected_cohort: Potentially temporary visa holders, international students and temporary graduates if adopted
observed_fact: Reuters reported an opposition proposal for substantial temporary-visa reductions and changes to student and graduate routes.
pathway_mechanism: Could affect expected route availability if enacted, but currently represents political uncertainty rather than a rule in force.
directional_eom_impact: Watchlist risk only; no baseline energy change.
counterfactual_or_caveat: Do not code proposal as implemented policy or treat the proposed numerical targets as observed outcomes.

change: Express Entry Comprehensive Ranking System changes announced for high-wage occupations
affected_cohort: Express Entry candidates with eligible Canadian work experience in high-wage occupations or a qualifying high-wage job offer; candidate must meet route-specific requirements
observed_fact: IRCC announced additional CRS points for eligible Canadian work experience or qualifying job offers in high-wage occupations; the two options are not combined. From 2026-11-03, LMIA will no longer be required for qualifying job offers used for these points and specified Federal Skilled Worker/Skilled Trades eligibility requirements. A high-wage occupation is defined as at least 1.3 times the median wage of the overall Canadian workforce.
pathway_mechanism: Could change relative invitation prospects for eligible candidates with Canadian work experience or qualifying high-wage offers; may alter employer/job-offer friction.
directional_eom_impact: Potentially lowers pathway-friction energy for the affected eligible cohort relative to other profiles; no numeric energy adjustment assigned.
counterfactual_or_caveat: Announcement is not yet effective on this run date. CRS points do not guarantee an invitation or permanent residence. Do not generalise to all migrants or occupations; no causal effect estimated.

change: Immigration and Asylum Bill 2026 factsheet details published
status: Bill/proposed reform; do not code as fully enacted policy
effective_date: Not applicable yet; implementation depends on legislation and commencement
affected_cohort: Refugees and people requiring humanitarian protection; asylum applicants and people affected by proposed appeals, Article 8 and modern-slavery reforms
observed_fact: Home Office factsheet describes proposed reforms including a single core-protection model for refugees/humanitarian protection, changes concerning Article 8 and modern slavery, and contributions toward asylum support where recipients can afford them.
pathway_mechanism: Could change expected protection, appeal, settlement and support conditions for humanitarian cohorts if enacted and commenced.
directional_eom_impact: Policy-uncertainty flag for humanitarian pathways only; no baseline energy change.
counterfactual_or_caveat: The source is a bill factsheet, not proof that all described provisions are in force. Separate publication date, legislative status and commencement dates; no causal effect estimated.
